lessons.subject: literature
lessons.lesson_title: AR Reading Launch: 60 Points per Semester
lessons.previous_learning: Atticus's close-reading comprehension is strong, while deeper explanations of why evidence improves an interpretation are still developing. The homeschool now adds a sustained independent-reading program alongside daily close reading.
lessons.course_context: Launch a semester-long AR-weighted independent reading goal using official Renaissance maximum point values as book weights.
learning_objectives: Select a semester reading book and read independently for at least 25 minutes.
Give a one-sentence update on what changed in the reading.
Build toward 60 AR-weighted points each semester.
Ask for quick vocabulary help without allowing one word to derail the reading session.
lessons.why_it_matters: Sustained reading builds vocabulary, stamina, background knowledge, inference, and readiness for demanding middle-school literature.

vocabulary.definition: a book weight based on Renaissance Accelerated Reader difficulty and length
a Renaissance measure of text difficulty
the ability to stay focused while reading for longer periods

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: your Semester 1 reading target is 60 AR-weighted points. Read at least 25 minutes on school days. Recommended Semester 1 books total 61 points: The Westing Game 8; The Giver 7; A Wrinkle in Time 7; Hatchet 7; Refugee 10; The Hobbit 16; The Crossover 2; Guts 4. To bank a book's full weight in our homeschool tracker, finish it, score 80%+ on a fresh comprehension check, and complete a short oral conference. Recommended first: The Westing Game. If an unfamiliar word does not block the sentence, mark it and keep reading. If it blocks meaning, ask for a quick plain-English definition and continue.

worked_examples.title: Reading without getting stuck
worked_examples.problem: You meet an unfamiliar word but still understand the scene.
worked_examples.solution: Mark the word lightly and keep reading.
worked_examples.explanation: Good readers protect the flow of the text and return to nonessential words later.

worked_examples.title: When to ask
worked_examples.problem: A word makes the entire sentence impossible to understand.
worked_examples.solution: Ask Virgil for a 10-second plain-English definition, then reread the sentence and continue.
worked_examples.explanation: Vocabulary support should help reading, not replace it.

independent_practice.prompt: Choose your current AR-weighted book. Read for at least 25 minutes. At the end, say one sentence: What changed or became clearer today?

exit_ticket.prompt: State the title you are reading, today's page range, and one thing that changed or became clearer.
exit_ticket.answer: A specific title, page range, and accurate one-sentence reading update.

lessons.voice_prompt: This is an independent reading block, not a lecture. Start by asking what book and page Atticus is on. Let him read silently for the planned time. If he asks what a word means, give a plain one-sentence definition and return him to the book. Do not over-explain. At the end ask only a short no-spoiler conference: What changed? What surprised you? What question do you have? Never pretend to administer an official Renaissance quiz. The homeschool uses verified AR maximum point values as book weights and its own comprehension checks.
lessons.teacher_notes: Semester 1 goal 60 points; current recommended list totals 61. Track reading daily and comprehension per finished book.
